subject: general
question: Let O be the centre of the circle and AB and CD are two parallel chords on the same side of the radius. OP is perpendicular to AB and OQ is perpendicular to CD. If AB = 10 cm, CD = 24 cm and PQ = 7 cm, then the diameter (in cm) of the circle is equal to:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The half-lengths of the parallel chords are 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm and 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm.

Notice the common Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13) where 13 represents the hypotenuse (radius).

The distances from the centre for these chords would be 12 cm and 5 cm.

Difference in perpendicular distances = 12 − 5 = 7 cm, which perfectly matches the given PQ.

Thus, the radius is 13 cm, meaning the diameter is 2 × 13 = 26 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Formula Used:**

A perpendicular from the centre to a chord bisects the chord into two equal halves.

Pythagoras Theorem: Hypotenuse² = Base² + Perpendicular²

**Calculations:**

⇒ AP = AB ÷ 2 = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm

⇒ CQ = CD ÷ 2 = 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm

⇒ Let the radius of the circle be r and the distance OQ = x.

⇒ Since chords are on the same side of the centre, OP = OQ + PQ = x + 7

⇒ In right-angled ΔOQC: r² = OQ² + CQ²

⇒ r² = x² + 12² = x² + 144 --- (i)

⇒ In right-angled ΔOPA: r² = OP² + AP²

⇒ r² = (x + 7)² + 5² = x² + 14x + 49 + 25 = x² + 14x + 74 --- (ii)

⇒ Equating (i) and (ii): x² + 144 = x² + 14x + 74

⇒ 14x = 144 − 74 = 70

⇒ x = 5 cm

⇒ Substitute the value of x in (i):

⇒ r² = 5² + 144 = 25 + 144 = 169

⇒ r = √169 = 13 cm

⇒ Diameter of the circle = 2 × 13 = 26 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 26 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Perpendicular from Centre to Chord

A perpendicular drawn from the centre of a circle to any chord bisects the chord into two equal halves. This forms a right-angled triangle where the radius is the hypotenuse.

Distance Between Parallel Chords

If two parallel chords lie on the same side of the centre, the distance between them is the difference of their perpendicular distances from the centre (d = |d₁ − d₂|). If they lie on opposite sides, the distance is the sum (d = d₁ + d₂).

Pythagorean Triplets in Circle Geometry

Commonly repeating triplets like (3, 4, 5) or (5, 12, 13) or (8, 15, 17) very frequently satisfy the values of the radius, half-chord, and perpendicular distance. Spotting them saves calculation time.
